Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

contdid 0.1.3

  • Sampling weights (weightsname) now work (#14). Previously they were accepted with a warning but had no effect. They enter the dose regressions, the comparison-group means, the averages over the dose distribution, the aggregation across timing groups, and the influence functions behind the standard errors, for both the dose aggregation and the event studies. dose_est_method = "cck" does not support weights and now gives an error.
  • Bug fix: ATT(d) and ACRT(d) from cont_did() with aggregation = "dose" were evaluated with a different B-spline basis than the one the dose regression was fitted with, unless dvals spanned exactly the range of the positive doses. With the default dvals (the 10% to 99% quantiles of the dose), the estimated dose-response curve was biased, most of all near the ends of the dose range. The basis now uses the range of the positive doses as its boundary knots everywhere (#16; thanks to @AsadGudzevic94).
  • Bug fix: with groups and time periods coded as calendar years, naming the group column G gave NaN estimates (ptetools #13). cont_did() now stores the dose as an internal column, so it never overwrites a user’s column, and selects each group-time subset using ptetools’ internal columns only.
  • anticipation now works: setup_pte_cont() did not pass it (or base_period and required_pre_periods) on to ptetools::setup_pte(), so groups without a valid base period were kept and estimation failed. cont_two_by_two_subset() now builds each cell with ptetools::two_by_two_subset(), so base periods, comparison groups and anticipation (in units of the time variable) follow did::att_gt().
  • A timing group with no more treated units than parameters in the dose regression now gives a clear error naming the group, instead of “something off with overall influence function” or “non-conformable arguments” (ptetools #17).
  • control_group and base_period are now used (#19, #10). They were not passed on to ptetools, so cont_did() always used not-yet-treated comparison units and a varying base period, whatever was requested. With a universal base period, the outcome change is now computed between the base and current periods matched by unit, which also works when the base period comes after the current one (pre-treatment cells).
  • clustervars now clusters standard errors (analytical and bootstrap) at a level above the unit, using ptetools’ new support (ptetools #6). It was previously ignored with a warning. It is not supported with dose_est_method = "cck".
  • bstrap = FALSE (analytical standard errors) is now passed on to ptetools; it was ignored, so the multiplier bootstrap was always used. Analytical standard errors are not available for dose-specific effects, where the bootstrap is still used (with a warning).
  • Bug fix: standard errors of ACRT (overall and event study) were too small by a factor equal to the share of treated units in each group-time cell (#13). The ACRT influence function was on the scale of the treated units only; it is now rescaled to all units, as for ATT(d). In simulations the reported SEs were about a third of the actual sampling variability before and match it now. Thanks to @AsadGudzevic94 (#17).
  • cont_did() now works with its default choice arguments (target_parameter, aggregation, treatment_type, dose_est_method, control_group), which are resolved with match.arg(). Before, each had to be set explicitly or the call failed an argument check (#12).
  • The ACRT can now be estimated when no unit is untreated, e.g. when every unit is treated at the same time with different doses (#5). It only involves derivatives of the dose-response curve, so it is identified from variation in the dose within each timing group. With target_parameter = "slope" and no untreated units, cont_did() now estimates it (with a message), for both aggregations and for dose_est_method = "cck". ATT(d) and the overall ATT are not identified without untreated units and are reported as NA; level parameters give a clear error when every unit is treated at the same time.
  • Fixed dose_est_method = "cck" with cband = FALSE: the ACRT(d) critical value stayed at the uniform-band value instead of the pointwise one.
  • control_group = "eventuallytreated" now works (ptetools #29): the comparison units are not-yet-treated units other than the never treated, and the latest-treated cohort serves only as a comparison group. It used to be silently treated as "nevertreated".
  • Repeated cross sections: cont_did() gains panel (default TRUE). With panel = FALSE, the level event study (target_parameter = "level", aggregation = "eventstudy") is supported, using ptetools’ repeated cross sections DiD estimator; idname is then not needed. The dose-specific estimators (ATT(d), ACRT) still need panel data (#7).
  • Require ptetools (>= 1.1.0), which fixes two problems with the standard errors of ATT(d):
    • The comparison-group part of the ATT(d) influence function had the wrong sign, so with ptetools 1.0.1 the standard errors of ATT(d) were too small and its confidence bands undercovered. In simulations, coverage of nominal 95% intervals is now about 95%.
    • The standard errors of ATT(d) and ACRT(d) are now computed with the same B-spline basis as the estimates. With older ptetools they would be too large near the ends of the dose range.

contdid 0.1.2

CRAN release: 2026-10-30

  • Bug fix: cont_did() with target_parameter = "level" and aggregation = "eventstudy" passed the continuous dose, rather than a treated/comparison indicator, to the underlying DiD estimator. This made the estimator weight treated units by their dose and put weight on some treated units in the comparison group, so event-study ATT estimates from earlier versions were biased when treatment effects are nonzero. With DRDID >= 1.4.0, which now requires a binary treatment indicator, this case failed with an error instead. Other combinations of target_parameter and aggregation were not affected.

contdid 0.1.1

CRAN release: 2026-07-21

  • Resubmission to CRAN following archival on 2026-07-16 (contdid was archived because its dependency ptetools had been archived; ptetools has since been restored to CRAN as version 1.0.1).
  • Require ptetools (>= 1.0.1) in Imports to prevent recurrence.
  • Update ggcont_did() to use ptetools’s autoplot() methods in place of the now-deprecated ggpte()/ggpte_cont().

contdid 0.1.0

CRAN release: 2025-07-03

  • Initial CRAN submission.
  • CCK estimation is working for case with two periods.
  • Change default parametric specification to cubic polynomial.
  • Bug fix for variable names.

contdid 0.0.002

  • Added sanity checks for unexpected input data.

contdid 0.0.001

  • Initial version.
